candidates.title: Plan-gate accept test skips the severity/title parity check its spec counterpart makes
candidates.detail: TestSpecReviewRoundCapAcceptOverridesAndMovesOn (cmd_answer_test.go:138) additionally asserts got.Items[0].Severity == "blocking" and .Title == "gap" to pin that finding detail (not just provenance) survives the carry. TestPlanReviewRoundCapAcceptOverridesAndMovesOn only checks Source and Gate (lines 160-162), so a regression that dropped severity/title while carrying the plan gate's finding would pass this test undetected. Low impact since the mechanism (carryFindings) is shared and already covered for the spec gate, but it's a minor asymmetry with the file's own stated goal of mirroring the spec family.

candidates.title: Dead os.IsNotExist tolerance in snapshotGateState
candidates.detail: snapshotGateState tolerates a missing gates/plan.json (`if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) { t.Fatal(err) }`), but its only two call sites (lines 192 and 197) run after planCapFixture, which drives three `review plan` rounds. cmd_review.go's recordReviewed (internal/cli/cmd_review.go:219-235, called unconditionally at line 193 regardless of verdict) always calls gate.WriteReceipt after every review pass, approve or rework, so gates/plan.json is guaranteed to exist by the time snapshotGateState is called. A project-wide grep for `snapshotGateState` (internal/cli/cmd_answer_plan_test.go:190,195) confirms no other caller exists that could hit this file before a plan receipt is written. The IsNotExist branch is therefore an unreachable defensive path — a plain os.ReadFile with t.Fatal on any error would say the same thing with less code.

verdicts.evidence: internal/cli/cmd_answer_plan_test.go's TestPlanReviewRoundCapAcceptOverridesAndMovesOn checks only `if got.Items[0].Source != gate.SourceOverride || got.Items[0].Gate != gate.Plan { t.Fatalf("provenance must survive: %+v", got.Items[0]) }` (lines 158-160) and then moves straight to the `next` dispatch assertion (line 161) — no assertion on `Severity`/`Title` anywhere in the file (grep for Severity|Title in the file returns no matches). Its spec counterpart, TestSpecReviewRoundCapAcceptOverridesAndMovesOn in internal/cli/cmd_answer_test.go, has the identical Source/Gate check at line 135 but adds `if got.Items[0].Severity != "blocking" || got.Items[0].Title != "gap" { t.Fatalf("finding detail must survive: %+v", got.Items[0]) }` at line 138. The asymmetry is real and verifiable: the plan test's own fixture (planCapFixture, cmd_answer_plan_test.go:54-55) constructs a rework finding with Severity "blocking" and Title "gap" but the accept test never checks those fields survived the carry, unlike the spec test which does.

snapshotGateState (internal/cli/cmd_answer_plan_test.go:171-182) tolerates os.IsNotExist on gates/plan.json: `planReceipt, err := os.ReadFile(...); if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) { t.Fatal(err) }`. A repo-wide grep shows its only two callers are both in TestPlanReviewRoundCapStopKeepsTheGateOpen, at lines 190 and 195, both invoked after planCapFixture (cmd_answer_plan_test.go:25-67), which drives three `review plan` rounds each ending in a rework verdict. runReview's recordReviewed (internal/cli/cmd_review.go:193, defined 219-236) is called unconditionally after every review pass regardless of verdict and always calls gate.WriteReceipt (gate.go:197-199), which writes gates/<gate>.json atomically. So gates/plan.json is guaranteed to exist by the fixture's first review round, well before either snapshotGateState call, making the `!os.IsNotExist(err)` branch unreachable for the code's only current call sites.
